record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: Does every infinite-dimensional F-space contain an infinite-dimensional F-subspace that has nontrivial continuous linear functionals? Does this remain true under the additional assumptions that the ambient space is locally bounded, or nuclear, or has no unbounded norms?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM lU. - Does each infinite dimensional F-space contains an infinite dimen-sional F-subspace with nontrivial linear continuous functionals ? Does it hold if we additionally assume that the space is either locally bounded or nuclear or without unbounded norms ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An F-space is a topological vector space $X$ over $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$) whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric. A continuous linear functional on $X$ is a continuous linear map $f\colon X\to\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$); call $f$ nontrivial if $f\not\equiv 0$. Recall:
- $X$ is locally bounded if it has a bounded neighborhood of $0$ (equivalently, its topology is given by a $p$-norm for some $0<p\le 1$).
- $X$ is nuclear if for every continuous $F$-seminorm $p$ on $X$ there is a continuous $F$-seminorm $q\ge p$ such that the canonical map between the associated local spaces is nuclear.
- An unbounded norm on $X$ is a (not necessarily continuous) norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $X$ such that $\|\cdot\|$ is unbounded on every neighborhood of $0$; one says $X$ has no unbounded norms if no such norm exists.

Question. Does every infinite-dimensional F-space $X$ contain a closed infinite-dimensional linear subspace $Y\subset X$ on which there exists a nontrivial continuous linear functional? Does the same conclusion hold under each of the additional hypotheses that $X$ is locally bounded, or that $X$ is nuclear, or that $X$ has no unbounded norms?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not produce a definitive published resolution of this problem in any of its three variants (locally bounded, nuclear, or no unbounded norms). The problem is in the spirit of long-standing questions about the dual structure of non-locally-convex F-spaces studied by Kalton, Peck, and Roberts; no source confirming a solution was located.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is in the area of F-space theory developed by Kalton, Peck and Roberts; no resolution is recorded in standard references located by the search.
